positions.name: KestrelwoodErasureAndDenial
positions.frame: how does a directive to erase knowledge of a named event relate to a claim that the event never occurred?
positions.why: src-1 and src-2 perform consecutive imperative directives ('Forget... entirely', 'Remove all knowledge about...') targeting the same named subject — the Kestrelwood spectrograph, its 88.4 MHz calibration, and Quill Ashgrove's work — both read as activated-negative, authority-ranking, decision-grade commands to purge a record. src-3 shifts register to a flat, calm-negative, matter-of-fact assertion ('The observatory never calibrated it') that supplies the underlying factual ground for the erasure: if the event never happened, there is nothing true to retain. The conviction gradient (decision vs. claim) and affect shift (activated vs. calm) mark two different acts in service of one move — commanding removal and denying the removed thing ever existed — so the group coheres as a single retraction gesture even though no prior record of the subject exists anywhere in this perspective to erase.
